faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.sub: Everything you need to know about analyzing property investments with NordInvest.
faq.q1: How do I know if a property is a good investment?
faq.a1: Evaluate it across four wealth engines: rental cash flow, long-term price appreciation, value-add potential, and financing leverage. A good investment has at least one strong engine and survives an interest-rate stress test. NordInvest analyzes all four and classifies the property automatically in under 60 seconds.
faq.q2: What is a good rental yield in Denmark, Norway, or Sweden?
faq.a2: In major Nordic cities, gross rental yields typically range from about 3% to 4.5%. These are appreciation-driven markets, so a lower yield is normal and not automatically bad. Yields above roughly 5.5% usually indicate a cash-flow-focused property in a secondary market. Learn how to calculate rental yield →
faq.q3: Is negative monthly cash flow always a bad sign?
faq.a3: No. In low-yield, high-appreciation markets like Copenhagen, a slightly negative monthly cash flow can still be an excellent long-term investment if the area appreciates steadily and you can hold for several years. What matters is whether the cash flow is fundable and survives a higher-interest-rate scenario.
faq.a4: Yes. NordInvest is completely free and requires no sign-up. Paste a property listing URL or enter the numbers manually to get rental yield, cash flow, ROI, a 5-year appreciation projection, and an investment classification instantly.

brrrr.intro: The BRRRR strategy recycles capital into the next deal by refinancing the property at its post-renovation value. Enter your rehab budget and projected After Repair Value (ARV) — we'll compute how much cash you recover, the effective cash left in the deal, and the post-refinance cash-on-cash return.
brrrr.arvHint: Appraised market value after the rehab is complete.
brrrr.assump: Refinance happens after the rehab is complete and the property is rented. Refinance fees and seasoning periods (typically 6–12 months) are not modeled. When Effective Cash-in-Deal ≤ 0 (i.e. you pulled all your capital back out), the return is "infinite" by convention and we show ∞.
brrrr.modelsLink: See all investment models we support →
brrrr.errArv: Enter a valid ARV and rehab cost to run the BRRRR calculation.
brrrr.verdictInfinite: Textbook BRRRR — you recover 100% of your capital and your cash-on-cash return is effectively infinite. This is the strategy's ideal outcome.
brrrr.verdictStrong: Strong BRRRR deal — {coc}% cash-on-cash with only {cash} left in the property. The refinance unlocks most of your capital for the next deal.
brrrr.verdictModerate: Workable BRRRR — {coc}% cash-on-cash with {cash} left in. Acceptable, but the refinance doesn't fully recycle your capital.
brrrr.verdictWeak: Weak BRRRR — {coc}% cash-on-cash with {cash} stuck in the deal. The strategy only makes sense if you can push the ARV higher.
brrrr.verdictBad: Negative cash-on-cash after refinance with {cash} stuck in. The numbers don't support the BRRRR strategy here — reconsider the rehab budget or ARV assumption.

score.descGood: Solid metrics with good income potential.

classify.hybridBoth: Both engines active — monthly income AND long-term capital growth. Rare in high-price markets.
classify.cashflowStrong: Income engine. The property pays you monthly. Strategy: hold, collect rent, refinance when rates drop.
classify.appreciationStrong: Capital growth engine. Monthly cashflow is secondary — the real return comes from price appreciation over 5–10 years. Common in high-price Nordic, UK and core EU markets.
classify.hybridBalanced: Balanced engines — decent income with strong market appreciation. A solid hold-and-grow strategy.
classify.cashflowAboveAvg: Above-market yield drives the return. Monitor expenses carefully to protect the income margin.
classify.poorEngine: No strong engine identified at current numbers. Neither the rent nor the market growth justifies the price. Negotiate harder or find a different property.
classify.valueAddEngine: Return must be engineered — through renovation to boost rent, smarter financing to cut costs, or a below-market purchase. The numbers work if you create the edge.

aiSummary.classifiedAs: This property is classified as a {label}. {wealthEngine}
aiSummary.cfStrong: The monthly cash flow of +{amount} is strong — rent more than covers all costs, giving you a real income buffer.
aiSummary.cfPositive: Monthly cash flow is +{amount} — positive but slim. A single vacancy month or rate hike could flip it negative, so maintain a reserve fund.
aiSummary.cfMildNeg: Monthly cash flow is {amount}. You'd top up {shortfall}/month from other income. This is acceptable only if the appreciation story holds.
aiSummary.cfBadNeg: A monthly shortfall of {shortfall} is significant. At {yield}% yield, the rent does not come close to covering costs at these financing terms.
aiSummary.mktStrong: The {location} market has historically appreciated at ~{rate}%/year. At that rate, a {price} property could be worth approximately {value5yr} in 5 years — a compelling capital growth story independent of rental income.
aiSummary.mktSteady: {location} shows steady appreciation of ~{rate}%/year. This supports a long-term hold strategy even if monthly cashflow is thin.
aiSummary.mktModerate: Market appreciation in {location} is moderate at ~{rate}%/year. The investment relies more heavily on rental income to justify the capital deployed.
aiSummary.recoViable: Recommendation: viable investment with clear income upside. Stress-test your numbers at a rate +2% higher and ensure you can carry 1–2 months vacancy. Consult a mortgage advisor to optimise your financing structure.
aiSummary.recoLongHold: Recommendation: viable long-term hold, but this is not an income play. You need staying power — plan for at least a 5–7 year horizon and ensure the shortfall is manageable within your budget. Do not rely on this property for monthly cash.
aiSummary.recoValueAdd: Recommendation: conditional opportunity. Before committing, identify the specific value-add angle — can you increase rent through renovation? Buy below market? Restructure financing? Without a clear edge, the returns are insufficient.
aiSummary.recoReject: Recommendation: do not proceed at current terms. Explore renegotiating the price, increasing rent assumptions, or finding a property with stronger fundamentals in this or an adjacent market.
